newsitem.title: USA: IndeNet begins rollout of digital system.
newsitem.headline: IndeNet begins rollout of digital system.

text.p: IndeNet Inc said Monday it has begun transmitting television commercials via its digital satellite network, putting the company two months ahead of its original rollout schedule.
By using IndeNet's network, advertisers can transmit their commercials to television broadcasters without having to copy videotapes and manually distribute them.
IndeNet said in a statement the benefits are improved quality, reliability, speed and verification of delivery.
TV commercials, or "spots" as they are called in the industry, are sent to stations that use IndeNet's Digital Spot Servers, receiver/decoders supplied by the company.
Each station is also supplied with an 18-inch satellite dish, which is aligned with Hughes Electronics Corp's geosynchronous Galaxy IV satellite, allowing for unattended 24-hour-a-day reception.
The system cuts broadcasters' overhead by eliminating tape transfer, tape storage, dish realignment and the personnel needed to receive physical tape deliveries, IndeNet said.
